children: The Democratic landslide in the U.S. midterms will change a lot in American governance, but not China policy--at least not in the short run, says Arthur Kroeber at Gavekal Research. Beijing and Washington's uneasy stalemate should persist, probably until the end of Trump's term. China lies far down Democrats' priority list, behind items such as inflation, AI regulation and the Iran war. "The party has no clear stance on China," divided by differing views of containment versus cooperation. "The Democrats will likely spend the next two years figuring out what China policy they want if they retake the White House, not trying to force big adjustments now." (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
